title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-olivia-martin.json
content:
PR: kv-cache + batching refactor (WIP)
Owner: Olivia Martin
Context: big refactor to unify KV cache retrieval and batching logic across gpt-family and llama-family models. Goal is to reduce duplicated cache lookups, enable continuous batching while preserving per-request latency SLOs.

Quick summary of concerns and TODOs:
- correctness: ensure KV cache hits for re-used prefixes are identical after refactor (edge cases: attention mask changes, past_key_values mismatch)
- latency regressions: batching layer currently introduces an extra copy per request; measure tail latency (p99.9) with existing load test harness
- memory: new aggregated cache structure may increase peak mem for long-conversation workloads; add memory accounting metrics
- fallback behavior: if cache store unavailable, route to warm cache mode (current behavior) — confirm tests cover this path

Review checklist (manual):
- [ ] validate unit tests for kv serialization/deserialization cover different dtype/quantized formats
- [ ] verify integration test: multi-tenant traffic with mixed sequence lengths 
- [ ] confirm metrics emitted: kv_hit, kv_miss, batch_size, batch_delay_ms, per-request-extra-copy_bytes
- [ ] ensure no blocking syscalls on hot path (fsync, sleep)
- [ ] check that telemetry contains trace id mapping back to original request for debugging

Files to focus on (PR diff pointers):
- runtime/kv/cache_manager.cpp/h (hot path changes)
- runtime/batching/batcher.cpp (new aggregated input handling)
- runtime/tests/kv_cache_integration_test.cpp (new fixtures)
- python/clients/compat_layer.py (minor glue changes for client headers)

Notes while skimming diffs:
- cache_manager: moved from per-request map to shared aggregated map; looks ok but:
  - line ~238 add() no longer clones buffer in the hot path; ensure buffer lifetime is guaranteed by caller
  - eviction callback signature changed; search for callsites in serving-runtime where old signature assumed sync evict
- batcher: introduced accumulate_until(size_or_timeout) API; potential deadlock when combined with existing scheduler if timeout==0
- tests: CI fixtures use small batch sizes (2) — need larger-scale e2e load to catch flakiness

Perf observations (local quick-run):
- baseline (pre-refactor) p95 token latency: 45ms, p99: 120ms under 200 rps
- after change (local quick-run with small batcher config) p95: 48ms (+6%), p99: 150ms (+25%) — need to validate under realistic multi-tenant settings

Follow-ups / action items:
- Immediate: add a test that simulates partial failures of cache store (timeouts, partial reads) and assert fallback path (Ethan)
- Short-term: run nightly load job (1000 rps, mixed seq lengths) against PR branch and capture metrics/trace (Lena)
- Medium: add memory metrics per-request and peak mem gauge to dashboard; create alert if 10% regression vs baseline
- Long-term: consider switching to pointer-based buffer ownership in add() to avoid copy; requires careful lifecycle reasoning and cross-thread safety

Open questions / design doubts:
- should batcher expose per-request deadlines to allow intra-batch priority reordering? (helps low-latency requests)
- how to handle model warmup interactions with prefix caches for streaming responses? currently streaming uses incremental KV writes that may race with cache reads
- security: are cache keys sufficiently namespaced for multi-tenant isolation? quick grep shows tenant_id included but double-check hashing function collision domain

Suggested reviewers:
- primary: Ethan Roberts (kv/cache), Lena Cho (batching/scheduler)
- secondary: Maya Thompson (integration tests), Samir Shah (perf)
